<!--
📌 One theme per pull request. If the title needs an "and", it is probably two
pull requests — and two small ones get reviewed faster than one large one.
-->

## What this changes

<!-- One or two sentences an outsider could follow. Lead with the plain-language
idea, then the mechanism. -->

Closes #

## Why

<!-- What breaks without it, concretely. Name the failure: "a 20 MB body gets
buffered whole and the box OOMs" beats "improves memory characteristics".

If the change is surprising, this is where you explain it. Anything that looks
wrong to a future reader but is deliberate needs the sentence that stops them
from "fixing" it back. -->

## Evidence

<!-- Not a checklist. Paste what you actually ran and what it printed.

`just ci` passing is the floor, not the evidence — it says nothing broke, not
that the thing you claim to have fixed is fixed. What we are looking for here
is the test that fails without your change:

  $ cargo +1.97.1 nextest run -p pingclair --test integration my_new_test
  ... with the fix reverted:
  FAIL [ 0.031s] my_new_test
  ... with the fix applied:
  PASS [ 0.028s] my_new_test

If you could not write a failing test, say so and say why. That is a legitimate
answer — an honest gap is far more useful than a green checkbox that means
nothing. -->

## Both transports?

<!-- Delete this section if the change cannot touch request handling.

H1/H2 (`server.rs`) and H3 (`quic.rs`) are separate execution paths, and
"fixed on one protocol only" is the defect this repository has repeated most.
Both arms existing does not mean both do the same thing.

  - [ ] Verified on H1/H2
  - [ ] Verified on H3
  - [ ] Parity is not required here, because: ... -->
